title: The energy cost of confining an electron
caption: Confining an electron to Δx forces a momentum spread of at least Δp = ħ/2Δx, so its kinetic energy is of order (Δp)²/2m, which grows as 1/Δx². For Δx = 0.1 nm, Δp ≥ 5.3 × 10⁻²⁵ kg m s⁻¹ and KE ≈ 0.95 eV: atomic energies. Squeezing to half the size costs four times the energy.
alt: Graph of minimum kinetic energy in electronvolts against confinement size from 0.05 to 0.5 nanometres: a steeply falling curve passing 0.95 eV at 0.1 nanometres.
description: The horizontal axis is the size Δx to which the electron is confined, in nanometres; the vertical axis is the minimum kinetic energy in eV.
At Δx = 0.1 nm the momentum spread is at least 5.3 × 10⁻²⁵ kg m s⁻¹ and the energy about 0.95 eV, the scale of atomic energies.
Halving Δx raises the energy fourfold.

checks.name: Δp ≥ ħ/2Δx gives KE ≈ 0.95 eV at 0.1 nm
KE falls as 1/Δx²: twice the size, a quarter of the energy
